thread:
Sabrina James: seeing a bug report on the Python streaming example (README + docs snippet). People paste it, tokens stream, but the final assistant message never prints / they think it “hangs” at the end.

In our current snippet we only print deltas and never handle the finalization event / final response object. If the last delta chunk is empty, you end up with no “final message” in logs.

Repro: run the example, you’ll see token output but no final “\n\nDone” or final content. Support is already getting questions.

Proposed fix: capture `response.completed` (or equivalent) and print the final assembled message, plus show how to get usage + finish_reason.

Ibrahim Khan: yep, I saw the same thing when testing snippet parity last week. It’s basically:
- we iterate events
- we `print(event.delta)`
- but we never call `stream.final_response()` / never show “final message object”

Also, if a user wants to store the message, deltas aren’t enough because tool calls / structured output won’t always be in the text deltas.

Wei Chen: +1. Docs page currently says “the last event contains the final message” which isn’t true for the SDK iterator (final is separate). We should be explicit:
1) stream deltas for UI
2) then fetch final response for persistence + usage

Monica Patel: can we get a PR up today? This is causing support churn and it’s a bad first-run experience.

Sabrina James: yep. Drafting now. The updated pattern:

```py
stream = client.responses.stream(
    model="redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
    input="Write a haiku about latency."
)

with stream:
    for event in stream:
        if event.type == "response.output_text.delta":
            print(event.delta, end="", flush=True)

final = stream.final_response()
print("\n\n---\n")
print(final.output_text)
print(f"finish_reason={final.finish_reason} usage={final.usage}")
```

(Names subject to whatever we settled in the canonical event taxonomy.)

Brian Murphy: from API side: yes, the “final message” lives on the completed response object. Streaming is incremental deltas + an explicit completion. We should avoid telling users to assume the last delta == final content.

Sahana Iyer: please add a snippet test so we don’t regress. We can assert that:
- we saw >=1 delta event
- `final.output_text` is non-empty
- stream closes cleanly

If you wire it into our mock server runner, we can avoid staging calls by default.

Ibrahim Khan: + also add a note for the common pitfall: people put `final = stream.final_response()` *inside* the `with stream:` block before the iterator finishes, which can block. We should show it after iteration.

Sabrina James: good call. I’ll add a comment in the snippet.

Connor O’Brien: release perspective: if this lands in python SDK, we should also make sure docs repo is updated to point at the new snippet. But immediate win is the SDK README.

Sabrina James: PR is up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk-python/pull/487
- updates README streaming example
- adds a regression test around “final response present”
- docstring clarifies delta vs final

Reactions: :thumbsup: (Monica Patel), :eyes: (Ibrahim Khan), :white_check_mark: (Sahana Iyer)

Ibrahim Khan: reviewing now. One nit: can we align event type string with the canonical naming we’ve been using in the Confluence draft? I think it’s `response.output_text.delta` in the SDK but docs sometimes say `output_text.delta`.

Sabrina James: updated in PR description + snippet to use the SDK’s actual `event.type` strings. Also added a tiny helper in test to fail loudly if the SDK changes the event name.

Wei Chen: can we add a 1-liner warning for docs:
“Deltas are for rendering; use the final response object for the authoritative text/usage.”

Sabrina James: added a short note right under the code block.

Sahana Iyer: snippet test looks good. I left a suggestion to also assert we saw a completion event (if exposed) — optional.

Monica Patel: thanks. Let’s merge + cut a patch release once CI is green. This is one of the highest-frequency “why is streaming missing the last message” issues.
